title: MXene-based composites: synthesis strategies, structure–properties relationship and emerging applications
content: MXenes have been developed as a versatile family of 2D transition metal carbides and nitrides, since their discovery in 2011, that possess metallic conductivity, a large specific surface area, tunable surface terminations, and strong M–C/M–N bonding. However, the utilization of them in the pristine state is limited due to restacking, poor flexibility and oxidative deterioration. The combination of MXenes with a second phase overcomes these constraints and leads to composites with significantly superior characteristics. This review explores the synthesis of MXenes, and fabrication, characteristics and applications of MXene/polymer, MXene/carbon and MXene/metal composites. First, the top-down etching approaches used to synthesize MXenes from MAX phases have been studied in terms of their merits and limitations. Then the principal fabrication techniques for each composite family have been covered and the resulting mechanical, thermal, electrical, and electrochemical properties of the fabricated composites. Additionally, the article emphasizes the performance of composites in energy storage, sensing, EMI shielding, water purification, and catalysis applications. Challenges specific to each composite family are discussed, followed by future directions covering the compositional space beyond Ti3C2Tx, green and scalable synthesis, intrinsic oxidation resistance, and safety, end-of-life, and techno-economic assessment. With ongoing advancement, MXene composites possess considerable promise for transition from experimental research to real-world implementation.
